C-RELEASE-ACTION-REFERENCES.Summary: Restore resolvable immutable action references in the release workflow and reject missing external action commits or metadata before merge.
C-RELEASE-ACTION-REFERENCES.Problem: The current release workflow has six uses of three commit SHAs that GitHub reports missing. Existing governance validates the 40-hex shape, not commit existence or action metadata. No release was dispatched to reproduce this configuration failure.

Goals.R-1: Replace the three unavailable action references with verified immutable commits whose action metadata and workflow-used inputs are compatible.
Goals.R-2: Add a bounded, read-only pre-merge reference check for external actions in the privileged release, promotion and governance workflows. Validate both commit existence and action metadata at the same exact SHA; syntactically valid missing SHAs must fail.
Goals.R-3: Keep deterministic offline fixtures for missing commits, missing metadata, unsupported inputs, local actions, subdirectory actions, duplicate references, API errors and bounded timeouts. Do not execute external actions to inspect them.

Constraints.Constraint: Preserve full-SHA pinning and the existing release-authorize, signing, approval, attestation, artifact-identity and publication boundaries. The change does not authorize or dispatch a release.

Candidate replacements, read from upstream major refs on 2026-11-11: tauri-apps/tauri-action 84b9d35b5fc46c1e45415bdb6144030364f7ebc5; actions/attest-build-provenance e8998f949152b193b063cb0ec769d69d929409be; sigstore/cosign-installer 398d4b0eeef1380460a10c8013a76f728fb906ac. Recheck exact metadata and required runner runtimes before approving the completed plan; mutable tags are discovery only.
Keep the current workflow inputs: Tauri args, attestation subject-path and Cosign cosign-release v2.4.1. Do not silently upgrade the installed Cosign binary or change artifact names.

Use GitHub's read-only API with least-privilege workflow permissions, bounded concurrency and an overall deadline including body reads. Never expose credentials in diagnostics, URLs or reports; never send an authorization header to a redirected host.
Offline tests inject transport responses and never contact GitHub. Network failure must produce an explicit non-green check result rather than a successful skip.
No production secrets, account controls, rulesets, release environments, versions, tags, dispatches or publication are changed.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Repairing manual-build artifact upload, Cargo cache paths or signing dependency isolation. They remain separate findings.
Automatically changing pins to moving tags, automatically trusting a major tag, executing third-party code during validation, or recursively auditing all dependencies inside each upstream action.
Proving end-to-end signed release execution from configuration validation.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Each chosen replacement has a successful commit lookup, action.yml or action.yaml at the exact commit, a supported action runtime and metadata declaring every input used by this workflow. Record public commit/metadata URLs.
The original three unavailable pins fail the new checker; the selected replacements pass. A generated all-zero 40-hex SHA also fails despite passing the old shape check.

Tests cover action references with and without a subdirectory, action.yml/action.yaml fallback, duplicate lookup coalescing, unsupported input, missing commit/metadata, malformed response, authentication/rate-limit/server failure, cross-host redirect and a response whose body stalls beyond the common deadline.

The workflow runs the reference check on ordinary relevant pull requests with read-only permissions and no release/signing credentials. Changes to any checked workflow or the checker cannot evade its selection rules.
Existing governance tests, deterministic pin rules and actionlint remain passing. Routed M-046/V-M-046 contracts and verification describe the additional read-only boundary.

AffectedAreas.Area: .github/workflows/release-governance.yml and its job-selection rules, only to run the bounded read-only check.
New tools/action-ref-check.mjs and tests/renderer/action-ref-check.test.js; tools/release-governance.mjs only if sharing the existing immutable-ref extractor requires it.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Offline failing-first missing-ref cases, exact replacement commit/metadata receipts and a green hosted pre-merge reference check on the proposed head. The completed plan measures leaf-command budgets and keeps online acceptance distinct from deterministic tests.

Assumptions.Assumption: The proposal is draft; candidate upstream SHAs are verified discovery results, not owner approval of executable third-party dependencies.
A new checker is bounded to current privileged workflows. Expansion to every workflow is a separate scope decision.
